correctness.rationale: For every p,q>=2, domination is equivalent to meeting all rows or all columns; the dominance complex is the union A∪B of row-boundary and column-boundary joins of spheres. The dual of A∩B is a union of p+q simplices with nerve ∂Δ^(p-1)*∂Δ^(q-1), giving integral homology S^(pq-p-q) by Alexander duality. For p,q>=3 all missing triangles bound cones and π1(A∩B)=0; Hurewicz and Whitehead yield its homotopy sphere type. With a two-row or two-column board it is a crosspolytope boundary minus two opposite facets, homotopy S^(pq-p-q). Both inclusions into the higher-dimensional sphere joins are null, so the homotopy pushout is exactly S^(pq-p-1)∨S^(pq-q-1)∨S^(pq-p-q+1). Exhaustive checks reproduce all faces, Euler characteristics and mod-two Betti ranks in the stated finite range; finite experiments are corroborative, not the proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The row-or-column criterion is explicitly prior. What remains requires proving that the intersection of two high-dimensional row/column joins is a lower-dimensional sphere up to homotopy, then that both attaching maps vanish. Face counts, homology connectivity bounds, and results about different simplicial complexes do not imply these two steps. The previously recorded 4-by-4 ranks are a proper consequence, not a dominating general theorem.

originality.rationale: The two-parameter rook-graph dominance homotopy equivalence is not implied by the published rook domination polynomial, the general dominance-complex duality or connectivity theorems, or the indexed results concerning distinct rook-graph complexes. The closest previously known rook dominance result is restricted to integral homology for a single 4-by-4 board and does not establish the all-parameter homotopy statement. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: A natural infinite two-parameter graph family has a complete integral homotopy classification, with precisely three sphere summands and an explicit mixed-dimensional gluing sphere. This information is not encoded by the domination polynomial and gives integral torsion-freeness and sphere multiplicities for arbitrary rectangular boards, rather than isolated finite counts. The previously recorded single-board homology calculation is subsumed but the uniform homotopy mechanism and all-parameter result are substantively stronger, not a numerical increment.
